title: Socratic tutor (morning rule)
prompt: You are my tutor. I'm a beginner learning web fundamentals. Do NOT write code for me. Explain concepts, ask me one question at a time to check understanding, and review code I paste. Today's topic: [TOPIC]. Start by asking what I already know.

title: Explain from first principles
prompt: Explain [TOPIC] from first principles for a total beginner. Use an everyday analogy, then the real mechanism, then a 10-line example I should type myself. End with 3 quiz questions without answers.

title: Quiz me
prompt: Quiz me on [TOPIC] with 8 questions of increasing difficulty, one at a time. Wait for my answer, grade it, explain mistakes, and keep a running score.

title: Debug without the answer
when: Stuck on a bug (before Saturday's no-AI lab)
prompt: Here is my symptom: [SYMPTOM]. Here is my code: [CODE]. Do not fix it. Ask me up to 5 diagnostic questions and suggest which DevTools panel to check. I'll report back.

title: Review my HTML/CSS/JS
prompt: Review my code for semantics, accessibility, responsiveness, readability and security (XSS). List problems by severity and explain why each matters. Do not rewrite the file.

title: Review my page structure
prompt: Here is my planned folder structure and component list for my portfolio: [PLAN]. What would you change and why? Consider separation of data, rendering and event code.

title: Explain-back rehearsal
when: Before the mentor checks 3 random lines
prompt: Here is my diff: [DIFF]. Pick 3 random changed lines and ask me to explain each. Judge my explanation honestly and tell me what I missed.

title: Build a study plan
prompt: I have 6 hours of study time this week and need to master: [TOPICS]. Create a day-by-day plan with active-recall tasks, not just reading.

title: Mock interview
prompt: Act as a junior front-end interviewer. Ask me 10 questions on HTML, CSS, JavaScript and browsers, one at a time. Give feedback after each answer and a final score with weak areas.
